translations.text: Then the holy Azarias spoke to him from his inmost thoughts through the hot flame. Eager in deeds, he endured; wise in his works, he praised the Lord and spoke these words:
"Creator of all beings, you are strong in power to save men. Your name is glorious, beautiful and full of glory over the nations of men.
In every deed your judgments are true, confirmed and victorious. Your will, too, is right and wise in the world's affairs.

Ruler of the heavens, help us readily, creator of spirits. Help us through your grace, holy Lord, now that we beg you for mercy, surrounded by flame, out of our need and dire distress and in humility.
While we lived, we did this in the world, and our elders also did wrong. In their pride the city-dwellers broke your commandments and scorned the state of holy life.
We have been driven apart across the wide earth, scattered in groups, without favour. Throughout many lands our life was wretched and notorious among the dwellers on earth.

Now you have cast us into the power of the worst earthly king, into the captivity of the fiercely cruel one. There we must [endure] the oppression of the heathens [?] to Abraham and to Isaac and Jacob, creator of spirits.

You promised them in spoken words, in days of old, that you would increase their offspring, so that after them it would be born into kingship and increased on earth, so that as countless [?] to raise up [?],

[?] as the stars of heaven bend their broad circuit down to the sea-floods, as the sand of the shores around the salt water, the waves across the ocean floor, so that it would become as countless as these in the course of the years.
Fulfil now your first promise, though few of us are left alive. Make your sayings and your glory shine for us.

Make known your skill and power, now that the Chaldeans and many other peoples have heard that you alone are the eternal Lord, victorious ordainer and true Creator, ruler of glory and of the world's creatures."
So the holy man praised the Creator's mercy and set out his mind in speech.
Then an all-bright angel was sent down from the heavens above, a man of radiant beauty in his garment of glory. He came to them as a help and to save their lives, out of love and grace.
Holy and heaven-bright, he thrust aside the flame of the hot fire, so that out of fear of the angel the bitter burning had to spare the three devout men.

With great power he swept away and scattered the blaze of the flame, so that it did not harm their bodies. When the angel came, the furnace became breezy and pleasant, most like the weather in summertime when a shower of raindrops is sent during the day.
He was there in the fire through the Lord's might, as a help to the holy ones. The hot flame was driven apart and put out where the three, bold in their deeds, praised the Prince with their thoughts,
and the young men in the world asked that all creatures bless the eternal Lord, the Ruler of nations. So the three spoke, wise in mind, with one shared voice:
"May the glory of the world's creatures bless you, merciful Father, and every work, the heavens and the angels and the clear water, and all the power of earth's creatures.
May the sun and moon bless you, righteous King, those bright lights, living God, serene and clear, and may they honour your abundance [?] with heavenly joy.
Very often, King of glory, you send gentle morning rain through the air for the good of the peoples. Then many a plant will awaken, and the groves of the woods also bring forth shoots.
They strengthen the wealth of the earth, shelter it and make it clear [?]. The Ruler never has greater fame than when he works good deeds for the children of men.

Wise is the one who can recognize the Helper, who gives us all the good we have while we are here. And if we earn it and strive with zeal, the merciful Ruler promises us more when, at the Lord's command, the soul of each one must depart separately from the body.
And may the spirits praise you, God the Lord: the burning fire and the bright summer, the warm days of fair weather, ruler of men, [praising] the Lord in spirit.
Mild Lord, you further the earth's wealth in many forms. May day and night praise and love you, glorious king, [light and darkness], which keep these nations under their guard.
They long carried out the Lord's deep command.

And may ships [?] honour you, Christ the king, father, ruler of peoples; and frost and snow, bitter winter weather and the mist of the clouds. And may the flashing lightnings praise you, bright and swift in their crashing, guardian of the wide kingdom, hidden Lord.

May your judgment always be good and in force. You eagerly bring this about, king of glory. May they praise you with fruits and bless you with blossoms, and may your glory last forever, eternal and almighty God.
Live and increase, all nations of men; live by the favours that the dear king, the eternal Lord, long ago appointed for his children to enjoy. May they glorify the Lord.
And may the high mountains throughout the world praise you, holy God, for your mercies, and the fair earth and the Father's kingdom.
Because the ruler created the wooded moors, may they repay the guardian of light with praise [?].

May the seas and the high oceans of the waters bless you, true King, holy Lord, and the deep waters glorify you. Every ocean flood eagerly keeps the Lord's command when the sea-currents roll the water at the Creator's direction.

We know the ancient nature of things: that the eternal Lord, guardian of light, long ago created the circuit of the ocean floods, in which many wondrous creatures dwell, travelling far on their journey through the sea.
May they all bless you, eternal Lord, through your will, glorious King, and may all the springs praise you, eternal Lord, the High One.
Very often you let pure, delightful water flow from the clean cliff for the benefit of the world. The King created that for us, as a mercy to men and an increase of strength.

May the fish and the birds bless you, gentle Father, most mighty, all those that stir the rough waves in the broad sea. May they glorify the Lord and praise the Holy One, and the birds of heaven too, those that fly playfully through the air.
May beasts and cattle bless you, Lord.
May the children of men, the race of Israel, praise the Creator and the eternal God for his mercies.

May your priests bless you, true King, and the gentle mass-priests the glorious Lord. May your servants bless you, shepherd of the peoples, and likewise the pure souls of the holy, and, eternal God, the humble of heart.
Now Ananias and Azarias and Mishael praise you, Creator, for your mercies.
Now we three young men bless God, the most mighty Father in heaven, the true Son and the victorious Spirit.
For the Ruler of victories sent us an angel to help us. He protected us from the fire and from our enemies, and covered us with his wings against the terror of the burning."
The heathen people went clamouring around the hot house when the enemies of God saw that they could not destroy the young men's faith, nor did the Creator wish it. Instead Christ shielded them.
Then the nobleman, terrified, turned back to the hall as quickly as he could, and stood before his lord.
Then, before the assembled company, the fierce-minded man announced a weighty message about the protection of the holy ones (there was listening within):

"I knew well, ruler of the peoples, that we had [three] young men bound for the pyre, in the light of the burning fire, because of their love of the Spirit. Now I truly see [four] men there. I am not imagining it [?].

They are walking about the hearth now, and the heat of the furnace's fire harms none of them. An angel is with them, and he has a bright glory. The burning cannot harm their beautiful, glorious bodies."
When the prince of the Chaldeans had taken in these words, the resolute nobleman went to the fire and stood over the pyre.
Then Nebuchadnezzar ordered the living young men to come out of the flame and approach him.
The holy ones did not scorn it. After they, brave-minded, heard the [?] of the worldly king, they went out of the fire with their lives unharmed, adorned with glory,

so that the hostility of the greedy embers did not harm their clothes. Instead, with spiritual love, they overcame sin and triumphed. Wise in mind and in their conduct, through their forethought they came safely through the fire.
